title: Bless'd Morning, Whose Young Dawning Rays
description: Bless'd Morning, Whose Young Dawning Rays in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 72, headed “The Lord's Day; or, The resurrection of Christ”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Bless'd morn-ing, whose young daw-ning rays Be-held our ris-ing God, That saw him tri-umph o'er the dust, And leave his dark a-bode.

lines: Bless'd morning, whose young dawning rays
That saw him triumph o'er the dust,
In the cold prison of a tomb,
Till the revolving skies had brought
Hell and the grave unite their force
To hold our God in vain,
To thy great Name, Almighty Lord,
Let heaven, and earth, and rocks, and seas,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
